## Adversarial Claim Verifier (voter 1/3)

Be SKEPTICAL. Try to REFUTE this claim. ≥2/3 refutations kill it.

## Research question
What are the best design patterns, layouts, typography, and UX principles for real-time operations TV dashboards (also called "big screen dashboards", "NOC dashboards", "control room dashboards", "retail operations monitors")? I need:

1. Layout principles: how to arrange KPIs, charts, status cards for a multi-store retail network dashboard meant to be watched on a TV/large monitor by the company owner
2. Typography best practices: font sizes, hierarchy, what's readable from 2-3 meters away
3. Color and visual hierarchy: how to use color for status (green/amber/red), when to use it, when NOT to use it
4. What data to show: for a retail food business (5 stores + 1 factory), what are the most critical real-time KPIs? Sales per store, comparatives, inventory alerts, production - what else is insightful?
5. Card design: best practices for individual store cards in a multi-store dashboard - what to include, what to omit, how to make it scannable in 2 seconds
6. Animation and live data: how the best dashboards handle real-time updates, counter animations, freshness indicators
7. Reference products/companies known for excellent dashboard design: examples from Datadog, Grafana, Retool, Vercel, Linear, Square, Toast POS, or any retail analytics dashboards
8. Anti-patterns: what makes dashboards bad (number overload, too many colors, unclear context, etc.)

Focus on actionable design decisions, not generic advice. We use glassmorphism with sage green (#57715B) on white background. The dashboard shows: live Degust sales per store, marketing actions, stock losses, inventory alerts, production data. Owner of a healthy sweets brand in Brasilia, Brazil monitors 5 stores + 1 factory.

## Claim under review
"The critical KPI set for retail store performance dashboards includes sales revenue, average order value, inventory on-hand/on-order, weeks of supply, conversion rates, profit margins, and category-level weekly sales trends."

**Source:** https://vidi-corp.com/store-performance-dashboards/ (blog)
**Supporting quote:** "Sales revenue and average order value, Inventory levels (on-hand, on-order units), Weeks of supply calculations, Customer retention and lifetime value, Conversion rates and profit margins, Category performance and weekly sales trends"

## Checklist
1. Is the claim actually supported by the quote, or is it an overreach/misread?
2. WebSearch for contradicting evidence — does any credible source dispute or heavily qualify this?
3. Is the source quality sufficient for the claim's strength? (extraordinary claims need primary sources)
4. Is the claim outdated? (check dates — old claims about fast-moving fields are suspect)
5. Is this a marketing claim / press release / cherry-picked benchmark / forum speculation?

**refuted=true** if: unsupported by quote / contradicted / low-quality source for strong claim / outdated / marketing fluff.
**refuted=false** ONLY if: claim is well-supported, current, and source quality matches claim strength.
Default to refuted=true if uncertain.

Structured output only. Evidence MUST be specific.

# Store Performance Dashboard KPIs

The article doesn't provide a single consolidated list of KPIs. Instead, it recommends different metrics for various dashboard types:

**Retail Store Performance Dashboard** (jewelry brand, POS-focused):
"Sales, Revenue, Average Order Value, and Number of Orders"

**Inventory Dashboard** (stock management):
"On-hand Units," "On-order Units," "Total Pipeline Units," "Weeks of Supply," and "Units Sold Per Store Per Week"

**Grocery Store Dashboard** (category analysis):
"revenue, units sold, average ticket price, profit, and profit margin"

**Amazon Dashboard** (e-commerce profitability):
"ACoS (Advertising Cost of Sales)" and "TACoS (Total Advertising Cost of Sales)"

The article emphasizes that "KPIs should align with business goals, such as increasing sales revenue or improving customer satisfaction," suggesting metrics vary by retail context and operational priorities.

Links: [{"title":"Retail Store Performance Dashboard: 6 KPIs and How To Track Them","url":"https://www.posnation.com/blog/retail-store-performance-dashboard-kpis"},{"title":"Retail KPIs: Essential Metrics to Boost Store Performance in 2025","url":"https://qoblex.com/blog/essential-retail-kpis-complete-guide-to-measuring-store-performance-in-2025/"},{"title":"Key Performance Indicators for Retail: 6 Essential KPIs Every Store Must Track | Hoxton AI Blog","url":"https://www.hoxton.ai/blog/essential-kpis-metrics-in-retail"},{"title":"Retail Performance Dashboard: The 10 KPIs Every Store Manager Should Track | Moonstar","url":"https://moonstar.ai/retail-performance-dashboard-10-kpis-store-manager/"},{"title":"16 KPIs and Metrics You Should Include in a Retail KPI Dashboard | Databox","url":"https://databox.com/retail-kpi-dashboard"},{"title":"19 Key Retail Reports & KPIs for Evaluating Store Performance (2025) - Shopify","url":"https://www.shopify.com/enterprise/blog/retail-reports"},{"title":"25 Retail KPIs & Metrics to Track | NetSuite","url":"https://www.netsuite.com/portal/resource/articles/financial-management/retail-kpis.shtml"},{"title":"Top 25+ Retail KPIs and Metrics for 2025 Reporting","url":"https://insightsoftware.com/blog/retail-kpis-and-metrics-for-reporting/"},{"title":"Retail KPI Dashboards: Tracking the Metrics that Drive Growth | by Xbyte Analytics | Medium","url":"https://medium.com/@seo.xbyteanalytics/retail-kpi-dashboards-tracking-the-metrics-that-drive-growth-242c599a5c4c"},{"title":"10 Essential Retail KPIs and Metrics for Growth in 2025","url":"https://www.usedatabrain.com/blog/retail-kpis-metrics"}]

Based on the search results, here's a comprehensive guide to retail store performance dashboard KPIs and best practices for 2024-2025:

## Key Metrics to Show

**Sales & Revenue KPIs:**
Website traffic and average purchase value are the two most important KPIs to measure in retail. Additional critical metrics include:
- Sales per square foot, which measures store size efficiency
- Conversion rate, which shows how well a store turns traffic into buyers
- Average transaction value (ATV), units per transaction (UPT), and attachment rate

**Inventory Management:**
Inventory turnover measures how many times you sell and replace your stock during a specific period.

**Customer Experience:**
Customer satisfaction scores, Net Promoter Score (NPS), and customer retention rates measure customer experience and loyalty.

**Leading vs. Lagging Indicators:**
Lagging indicators like net profit and year-over-year growth tell you what already happened. Leading indicators like conversion rate and foot traffic predict future performance. A balanced KPI dashboard includes both types.

## Dashboard Design Best Practices

**Keep It Focused:**
Limit your primary dashboard to 5-7 key metrics to maintain focus. Limit to 6–8 key KPIs per view.

**Three-Tier Structure:**
Design your dashboard around three tiers of information, with your most important KPIs displayed with clear visual indicators showing current status and trend direction, including net sales (current period vs. target and prior year).

**Add Context & Comparisons:**
Include comparison benchmarks wherever possible, showing current performance against the same period last year, against targets, and against company averages.

**Drill-Down Capability:**
Enable clicking on any summary metric to reveal detailed breakdowns by product, location, time period, or other relevant dimensions, allowing managers to investigate anomalies without cluttering the main view.

## Implementation Best Practices

**Regular Monitoring:**
Wait two to three months to analyze the results and look for trends, then set benchmarks and goals you hope to achieve six months to one year from now.

**Data Integration:**
When data flows seamlessly from your sales channels, warehouses, and accounting software into unified dashboards, you spend less time gathering information and more time acting on insights.

**Focus on Actionability:**
The most useful retail KPIs are the ones managers can understand, explain to teams, and influence through better execution. They should be simple enough that teams actually care about them and specific enough that managers know what to do next.

I now have enough evidence to evaluate the claim. Let me analyze the findings.

**Assessment:**

1. **Source quality check:** The vidi-corp.com source is a vendor blog (Vidi Corp sells dashboard software). It is a marketing-oriented source, not an academic or industry-standard reference. This is a low-to-medium quality source for asserting "the critical KPI set."

2. **Quote vs. claim mismatch (critical finding):** The WebFetch of the actual source page reveals the claim significantly **overreaches the quote**. The article does NOT present a single unified "critical KPI set." Instead, it breaks KPIs across completely different dashboard types:
   - Sales/AOV are from a jewelry brand POS dashboard
   - Inventory on-hand/on-order/weeks of supply are from a separate **inventory dashboard**
   - Profit margins are from a **grocery store** category dashboard
   - Conversion rate is not prominently featured as a "critical" standalone KPI in the article
   
   The claim merges these distinct, context-specific lists into one universal "critical set" — which the source does not support.

3. **Contextual mismatch for food retail:** Multiple authoritative sources (Shopify, NetSuite, Databox, Moonstar) confirm that conversion rate and customer lifetime value are primarily applicable to general retail with foot traffic measurement. For a food/QSR context like healthy sweets (Momma), these metrics are either inaccessible in real-time or not primary operational KPIs. Foot traffic sensors are rarely standard in small food retailers.

4. **"Profit margins" as real-time TV dashboard KPI:** Credible sources consistently distinguish between operational/real-time KPIs (sales revenue, transaction count, AOV) and analytical/strategic KPIs (profit margins, CLV, category trends). Profit margin requires cost data that is rarely available in real-time POS streams. Showing it on a TV dashboard is an anti-pattern per dashboard design literature.

5. **Weeks of supply on a real-time ops dashboard:** This is an inventory planning metric, not a real-time operational one. Its inclusion in a "critical KPI set" for a live operations TV dashboard conflates planning analytics with operational monitoring.

input.evidence: The claim overreaches the source in two critical ways. First, the vidi-corp.com article does NOT present a single unified "critical KPI set" — WebFetch of the actual page confirms it separates KPIs across four distinct dashboard types (jewelry POS, inventory management, grocery category, and Amazon e-commerce). The claim fuses these context-specific lists into one universal set, which the source does not support. Second, the source is a vendor marketing blog (Vidi Corp sells dashboard software), a low-quality source for asserting a universal "critical" standard. Beyond the source problem, the specific KPIs named are problematic for the stated use case: (a) Conversion rate requires foot-traffic sensors not standard in small food retail; (b) Profit margin requires real-time cost data rarely available in POS streams and is consistently classified by authoritative sources (Shopify, Databox, NetSuite) as a strategic/analytical metric, not an operational dashboard KPI; (c) Customer retention/CLV and weeks-of-supply are planning metrics, not real-time operations metrics appropriate for a TV dashboard. The claim conflates operational real-time KPIs with strategic and planning KPIs, treats a fragmented vendor blog list as a universal standard, and the supporting quote does not actually back the unified claim.
